details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> metal : CONV_2D tensor API for M5, split-K for all chips (#32542) * metal: add a tensor API conv_2d kernel and split long reductions The conv_2d matmul kernel runs on simdgroup matrices only, and gives each threadgroup the whole reduction of its output tile. On M5 this leaves the tensor cores unused, and convolutions with few output positions and a long reduction (IC * KW * KH in the thousands) run a handful of threadgroups on an otherwise idle GPU. Add kernel_conv_2d_mm_tensor for devices with the tensor API: like kernel_mul_mm, it gathers the patches of 64 output positions into threadgroup memory as the left operand and reads the kernel rows from device memory as the right operand. Devices without the tensor API keep the simdgroup kernel. details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> llama: fixes for Inkling 2 attention mask (#32429) * llama : give Inkling2 its own relative-position attention input The Inkling2 graph built its flash attention mask from the hybrid iswa input and passed it to build_attn through a new kq_mask argument. That argument let a caller pair its own dense mask with the kv_rows of llm_graph_input_attn_kv_iswa, whose mask follows the per-sequence cell lists whenever kv_rows is enabled. Add llm_graph_input_attn_rel_pos instead. It owns dense KQ masks and the query-to-cell distances, fills both from the same cells, and its build_attn overload adds the per-head bias to its own mask and never passes kv_rows. The iswa build_attn is back to its previous signature; its body moves to build_attn_iswa_impl, which both overloads call. Inkling2 now folds the per-query sink into the bias with and without flash attention, so build_attn_mha no longer needs the per-query sink path. Assisted-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * inkling2
